Okay! Imagine you have a long, straight stick in space, and you spin it around really fast. Now, if the stick is not perfectly balanced—like if it’s a little heavier on one side—the way it spins will start to look really weird. Instead of just spinning in a straight line, it starts to flip and twist in funny directions, kind of like a tumbling toy.

This happens because in space, there’s no air or ground to stop it, so when the stick spins and wobbles a little, it keeps changing the way it spins. This is called the Dzhanibekov Effect! It’s like when you spin a pencil in the air and it starts to wobble and flip instead of just going round and round.
